mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has risen monotonically from -53.1% (t-2w) to -40.6% (t-0w), a 12.5-point recovery trend. This sustained improvement in retail mobility signals restoration of consumer confidence and habit formation. The trend will persist over the next four weeks, producing higher mean RETAIL_REC than the prior four-week baseline.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC improved 12.5 points over three weeks
failure_condition: Mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is equal to or lower than the mean over the prior 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility has recovered from -43.9% (t-2w) to -24.1% (t-0w), a 19.8-point gain. This signals outdoor activity substitution and reduced lockdown compliance. Consumers emboldened by outdoor mobility will extend their activity radius to retail venues within two weeks, driving RETAIL_REC upward.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises more than 15 points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS improved 19.8 points from t-2w to t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to increase over the next 14 days despite PARKS remaining above -30%.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT mobility has stabilized near -37% (t-0w), down only 3 points from t-1w. When transit stabilization occurs alongside WORKPLACES stabilization near -36%, commuting routines lock in. Locked-in commuting drives weekday retail foot traffic. Over four weeks, this produces higher RETAIL_REC than baseline.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT week-on-week change is less than 5 points AND WORKPLACES week-on-week change is less than 5 points
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT at -37.1%, WORKPLACES at -36.4% in t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days does not exceed the prior 28-day mean, or TRANSIT or WORKPLACES resume sharp declines.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM has recovered from -28.6% (t-2w) to -18.9% (t-0w), a 9.7-point gain. This signals relaxation of essential-only restrictions. As essential-trip constraints ease, consumers will bundle retail and recreation with grocery trips. RETAIL_REC will rise within one week as trip bundling increases.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM rises more than 5 points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM improved 9.7 points from t-2w to t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase within 7 days of GROCERY_PHARM rising above -20%.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL mobility has declined from 14.3% (t-2w) to 9.9% (t-0w), a 4.4-point drop. Declining residential overstay signals consumers are spending more time outside the home. This behavioral shift will accelerate retail mobility within two weeks as outdoor time allocation increases.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL at 9.9% in t-0w, down from 14.3% in t-2w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase over the next 14 days, or RESIDENTIAL rebounds above 12%.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES and TRANSIT have both stabilized within a 1-2 point range over the last two weeks (WORKPLACES: -37.3% to -36.4%; TRANSIT: -40.0% to -37.1%). Dual stabilization indicates commuting equilibrium. When commuting equilibrium holds for two weeks, retail foot traffic follows within four weeks as work-trip anchors stabilize consumer schedules.
candidate_trigger: both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT show week-on-week volatility less than 3 points for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES range -37.3% to -36.4% over t-1w to t-0w
fact:TRANSIT range -40.0% to -37.1% over t-1w to t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than or equal to the prior 28-day mean, or either WORKPLACES or TRANSIT declines by more than 5 points.

mechanism_narrative: All mobility categories except RESIDENTIAL show consistent recovery patterns over the three-week window (RETAIL_REC +12.5 points, PARKS +19.8 points, GROCERY_PHARM +9.7 points, TRANSIT +3.3 points, WORKPLACES +1.3 points). This broad-based recovery indicates seasonal or policy-driven reopening. The recovery momentum will sustain RETAIL_REC gains over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: all non-residential mobility categories show positive week-on-week change for at least two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:broad-based recovery across all categories from t-2w to t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days does not exceed the prior 28-day mean, or any major mobility category reverses by more than 10 points.

mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC at -40.6% (t-0w) remains severely depressed despite recent gains. PARKS recovery to -24.1% and RESIDENTIAL decline to 9.9% indicate consumers are reallocating time away from home but toward outdoor recreation, not retail. This substitution will persist, keeping RETAIL_REC below baseline over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS recovery exceeds RETAIL_REC recovery by more than 10 points AND RESIDENTIAL remains below 11%
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days exceeds the prior 28-day mean, or PARKS mobility falls below -30%.
